question: What is the primary purpose of placing individuals in quarantine?

options.A: To provide permanent shelter for chronically ill patients
options.B: To separate healthy exposed persons to prevent disease spread
options.C: To treat active symptoms of a diagnosed infection
options.D: To conduct terminal disinfection of contaminated personal items

explanation: Quarantine is specifically applied to individuals who are currently well but have had exposure to a contagious pathogen, keeping them away from the general public until the incubation period passes. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h1)

question: How is the duration of a quarantine period scientifically determined?

options.A: By the administrative schedule set by local municipal authorities
options.B: By the total number of hospital beds available in the region
options.C: By the average recovery time of patients admitted to the intensive care unit
options.D: By the longest known incubation period of the specific infectious agent

explanation: The timeline for restricting movement is strictly dictated by how long the pathogen takes to manifest symptoms after initial exposure. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h1)

question: Which population is targeted by isolation protocols?

options.A: Individuals who are confirmed to be infected with a contagious disease
options.B: Community members living near an outbreak zone with no known contact
options.C: Healthcare workers who have completed their shift in a high-risk ward
options.D: Healthy travelers arriving from countries with low immunization rates

explanation: Isolation separates individuals who are already sick and infectious from those who are healthy to stop active transmission chains. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h2)

question: A patient with laboratory-confirmed Lassa fever is placed in a negative pressure room. This intervention is best described as what?

options.A: Quarantine because it involves a dangerous viral pathogen
options.B: Prophylaxis because it prevents secondary complications
options.C: Social distancing because it limits visitors to the ward
options.D: Isolation because the patient has an active, confirmed infection

explanation: Because the patient is actively sick with a confirmed disease, separating them from others constitutes isolation rather than quarantine. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h2)

question: What defines the incubation period of an infectious disease?

options.A: The total duration a patient remains contagious after full recovery
options.B: The timeframe required for antibiotic therapy to eradicate a virus
options.C: The time between pathogen exposure and the onset of clinical symptoms
options.D: The speed at which a bacterium multiplies on artificial agar plates

explanation: The incubation period represents the silent phase before clinical manifestations emerge, which is the exact window quarantine targets. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h3)

question: Why can an exposed individual transmit an infection during quarantine despite having no symptoms?

options.A: Asymptomatic carriers never develop antibodies against the disease
options.B: They may be shedding the infectious agent during the incubation window
options.C: Environmental toxins mimic the pathogen and trigger false positives
options.D: Their immune system is actively destroying the pathogen too quickly

explanation: Many contagious agents replicate and shed before clinical signs appear, making asymptomatic transmission a primary threat managed by quarantine. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h3)

question: What characterizes facility-based quarantine compared to home quarantine?

options.A: It utilizes centralized government-designated locations for groups
options.B: It allows unrestricted movement within public market areas
options.C: It is reserved exclusively for patients with severe acute respiratory failure
options.D: It is managed by individuals inside their own private apartments

explanation: Facility-based quarantine houses exposed individuals in managed centralized spaces rather than their private homes. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h4)

question: When is compulsory quarantine legally invoked by public health authorities?

options.A: When voluntary compliance by exposed individuals fails or is deemed unreliable
options.B: During the annual clearance of hospital pharmaceutical inventory
options.C: As a routine requirement for all newly hired nursing staff
options.D: Whenever a single routine vaccination appointment is missed

explanation: Compulsory measures are legal mandates used when voluntary adherence is insufficient to protect public health and safety. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h4)

question: Which of the following is a primary public health trigger for instituting quarantine?

options.A: An outbreak of a novel, highly contagious pathogen with pandemic potential
options.B: A seasonal increase in uncomplicated iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: The routine quarterly maintenance of municipal water purification plants
options.D: An isolated case of chronic degenerative joint disease

explanation: Quarantine is deployed for serious, contagious threats that possess the capacity to rapidly overwhelm healthcare systems and spread widely. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h5)

question: What factor do public health officials prioritize when deciding whether to enforce population quarantine?

options.A: The aesthetic appeal of the designated housing facilities
options.B: The transmission mode and severity of the infectious agent
options.C: The personal travel preferences of the exposed individuals
options.D: The market price of commercial cleaning supplies

explanation: Officials weigh how easily a pathogen spreads and how severe the resulting disease is to justify restricting movement. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h5)

question: Which federal agency plays a central role in coordinating public health responses and disease containment in Nigeria?

options.B: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

explanation: The NCDC is the national public health institute tasked with leading disease surveillance, preparedness, and outbreak response across Nigeria. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h6)

question: What ethical principle justifies the enforcement of quarantine during a severe disease outbreak?

options.A: Beneficence and the protection of collective community safety
options.B: Elimination of all documentation requirements for travelers
options.C: Complete individual autonomy regardless of public risk
options.D: Financial profit optimization for local health facilities

explanation: Ethical frameworks justify restricting individual movement when necessary to protect the wider population from catastrophic harm. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h6)

question: What is a core clinical responsibility of a nurse monitoring individuals in quarantine?

options.A: Administering terminal surgical procedures for chronic conditions
options.B: Conducting forensic autopsies on deceased community members
options.C: Issuing international passports and travel visas
options.D: Performing daily symptom screenings and temperature checks

explanation: Regular physiological tracking allows nurses to detect the earliest indicators of infection during the incubation period. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h7)

question: Why must nurses evaluate the psychological well-being of individuals undergoing quarantine?

options.A: Depression automatically grants immunity against viral pathogens
options.B: Mental instability prevents the human body from producing white blood cells
options.C: Psychological evaluations replace the need for physical temperature logging
options.D: Confinement frequently triggers anxiety, frustration, and emotional distress

explanation: Isolation and restricted movement take a heavy psychological toll, requiring nurses to monitor and support mental health during confinement. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h7)

question: Which action is critical to prevent a quarantine facility from amplifying disease transmission?

options.A: Strict adherence to infection prevention and control protocols
options.B: Storing biomedical waste in open corridors for easy access
options.C: Eliminating all handwashing stations to conserve water supplies
options.D: Permitting unrestricted daily visits from community members

explanation: Rigorous IPC measures, including PPE use and waste management, ensure that the containment site itself does not spread the infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing clear spatial zoning within a quarantine facility?

options.A: To simplify the architectural design blueprints for construction engineers
options.B: To ensure that administrative staff have larger bedrooms than quarantined guests
options.C: To separate clean administrative areas from contaminated zones and prevent cross-contamination
options.D: To reduce the overall electricity consumption of the facility

explanation: Zoning creates physical boundaries that protect healthcare workers and clean areas from exposure to infectious pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h8)

question: What is an immediate consequence of failing to provide adequate psychosocial and informational support during quarantine?

options.A: Automatic extension of the incubation period for all pathogens
options.B: Increased risk of resistance, anxiety, and breaches of containment
options.C: Accelerated physical healing and improved metabolic function
options.D: Immediate eradication of the infectious agent from the environment

explanation: Without clear communication and emotional backing, individuals often experience high anxiety and may attempt to leave quarantine prematurely. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h9)

question: Which nursing intervention best fosters compliance among individuals confined to a quarantine facility?

options.A: Providing clear education, reliable communication channels, and meeting basic physical needs
options.B: Isolating residents completely from any form of news or external contact
options.C: Restricting food and water intake to encourage faster symptom resolution
options.D: Refusing to answer questions regarding the expected duration of confinement

explanation: Trust is built when nurses address physical needs, answer questions transparently, and maintain open lines of communication. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h9)
